methodological_rigor.justification: This is a global, randomized phase III trial with 1:1 allocation via interactive response system and stratification by IGHV mutation status and Rai stage, comparing continuous pirtobrutinib to fixed-duration BendaR (Methods; Study Design and Treatment). The primary endpoint (IRC-assessed PFS) is defined with blinded independent review to mitigate open-label bias, and crossover is prespecified for control-arm patients with IRC-confirmed progression (Methods; Study Design and Treatment; Study Assessments). Statistical planning includes event-driven power assumptions, alpha control for OS contingent on PFS significance, and appropriate time-to-event analyses (stratified log-rank/Cox, reverse KM follow-up), with exposure-adjusted safety incidence to handle differential treatment duration (Methods; Statistical Analysis).

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: The trial directly compares an oral BTK inhibitor strategy against a commonly used frontline chemoimmunotherapy regimen in untreated CLL/SLL and reports a large PFS benefit with interim OS trends (Abstract; Results). As an individual randomized phase III study, it corresponds to Oxford LoE 1b (Methods). The findings are immediately clinically relevant for frontline decision-making, acknowledging exclusions (eg, del(17p)) that limit generalizability (Discussion; Limitations).

reporting_quality.justification: CONSORT applies, and the manuscript reports randomization/stratification, primary and secondary endpoints, ITT efficacy set, safety set definition, and key statistical methods including alpha allocation and stratified analyses (Methods; Statistical Analysis). It also provides trial registration (ClinicalTrials.gov identifier) and a data cutoff date (Methods). The normalized text does not include a data or code sharing statement, and protocol-level details are referenced as being available separately (Methods), so reproducibility artifacts are limited in the provided document.

novelty_literature.justification: The study is described as the first prospective randomized phase III evaluation of a noncovalent BTKi (pirtobrutinib) specifically in treatment-naive CLL/SLL versus BendaR (Discussion). It extends prior pirtobrutinib evidence from relapsed/refractory and post-cBTKi settings into the frontline population (Introduction). While BTKi class efficacy is established, the noncovalent agent and comparator design provide a notably novel contribution.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is organized with clear endpoint definitions, statistical methods, and quantitative reporting of HRs, CIs, and follow-up (Abstract; Methods; Results). Safety reporting accounts for differing exposure duration via exposure-adjusted incidence rates, improving interpretability (Methods; Statistical Analysis). Some operational details are referenced as being in the protocol/appendix, but overall presentation is clear.

key_strengths: Randomized phase III design with stratified allocation and blinded independent review of the primary PFS endpoint.
Strong statistical planning including event-driven powering, alpha control for OS, and appropriate stratified time-to-event analyses.
Clinically meaningful efficacy with careful safety handling via exposure-adjusted incidence given unequal treatment duration.
key_concerns: Open-label design and substantial crossover can complicate OS interpretation (OS noted as interim/immature).
Exclusion of del(17p) limits generalizability to higher-risk newly diagnosed patients.
No explicit data/code sharing statement is visible in the normalized manuscript.
chief_reviewer.rationale: High-quality randomized evidence with strong clinical impact and rigorous endpoint adjudication supports tier-1 plausibility, with remaining issues largely around generalizability, OS maturity, and transparency artifacts.
